text:
harry: Heads-up  proposing a quota-aware fallback mode for rollouts. idea: fallback decisions consume a small "quota token" per degraded request so orgs and routes can't exceed budget silently.

leela: interesting. that addresses cost runaway. how do tokens get priced? per-token cost = estimated extra compute + model delta?

dmitri: pricing aside, engineering Q: token issuance needs to be realtime and cheap. suggest token-bucket in the routing plane with async reconciliation to billing. no external RPC on request path.

sofia: UX: show a tiny token counter in the console per-org and per-route. when low, fallback preview should reflect throttle behavior. show tooltip: "tokens left in rolling window".

harry: proof-of-concept flow: 1) route gets N tokens per window (configurable). 2) each fallback consumes 1 token (or fractional). 3) when tokens exhausted, system either: a) stop degrading (hard stop), b) soft-throttle degrade rate, or c) fall back to a cheaper mode that costs 0 tokens. chooseable per-org.

leela: add a "grace credits" bucket for emergency ops (platform-admin can give +x tokens) with audit trail and optional 2FA.

ops-bot: deploybot: scheduled canary for quota-token bookkeeping on staging at 22:00 UTC :rocket:

dmitri: telemetry/implementation note: emit compact breadcrumb with token info so we can later reconcile. example: ```json
{"r":"latency","f":"lite","s":0.66,"tid":"t9x","tokens_left":42}
```

audit-bot: audit-bot: please ensure tokens_left is recorded as a numeric field in audit exports. emergency grants must include approver id and reason.

sofia: console UX: show an "estimated token burn" column in rollout preview. if operator increases aggressiveness, preview updates to show tokens/day used and an estimated exhaustion time. include a small "cost estimate" link.

harry: edgecases: multiple tiers (org, team, route). tokens should cascade: route uses route tokens then team then org. if none left, follow the configured exhaustion behavior.

leela: for previews we should simulate cascade behavior and surface where tokens would be pulled from so operators don't get surprised. e.g., "Route: billing will pull from team pool once route tokens exhausted".

dmitri: data storage: breadcrumbs stay compact. keep full traces when tokens_left jumps unexpectedly (eg sudden drop) or when operator clicks investigate. default full trace retention 21d, crumbs 365d.

harry: debate: should token consumption be visible in real-time metrics? ops teams want alerts when token burn > threshold. but flood risk again. propose aggregated alerts: emit alert when tokens_burn_rate > threshold for 1m.

sofia: +1 aggregated alerts. also add lightweight heat-dots next to counters for recent spikes. clicking opens small list of sample crumbs.

leela: API design: add fields to rollout policy resource: {"token_policy": {"window_s":3600,"tokens":10000,"exhaust_behavior":"soft_throttle|hard_stop|cheap_fallback"}}. document backwards compatibility.

dmitri: make exhaust_behavior enum; default to soft_throttle. soft_throttle = probabilistic degrade reduction to keep ~10% of prior degraded-rate. must be deterministic based on request hash to avoid bias.

harry: audit requirements: grants and manual overrides must be immutable and exportable with approver id. breadcrumbs should include audit_id linking back to grant events.

ops-bot: deploybot: dry-run will tag events with sim=true and emit sample breadcrumbs to staging logs.

leela: action items: 1) @dmitri prototype in routing plane (token-bucket + async reconciler). 2) @sofia mock console counters + exhaustion modal (Figma). 3) @harry draft product spec and exhaustion defaults. 4) @leela list alert thresholds and notification channels. 5) @audit-bot produce required audit export fields.

dmitri: I'll spin up a branch and post results from a 1h canary sim.

harry: one more UX thought: when tokens low, show proactive recommendation: auto-scale dedicated pool or switch to cheaper fallback until tokens replenish. let operators auto-apply with one-click (logs a grant if applied).

sofia: make auto-apply opt-in per-org. default is recommend-only. microcopy: "Recommend action: purchase more tokens or switch to cheaper fallback. Auto-apply will perform action and log audit event."

leela: sounds good. aiming to demo in next platform sync. thanks team :thumbsup:
